text.en: A treasure map says go 3 steps east and 2 steps north. A pair of numbers can name any place on a flat sheet. This is the idea of coordinates.

Two number lines cross at right angles. The horizontal one is the x-axis and the vertical one is the y-axis. They meet at the origin O with coordinates (0, 0).
A point is written as (x, y). The x-coordinate or abscissa tells how far to move along the x-axis. The y-coordinate or ordinate tells how far to move up or down. So (3, 2) is 3 right and 2 up.
The axes divide the plane into four quadrants. Quadrant I has x > 0 and y > 0. Quadrant II has x < 0 and y > 0. Quadrant III has both negative and Quadrant IV has x > 0 and y < 0.
A point on the x-axis has y = 0 and a point on the y-axis has x = 0. The order matters, so (3, 2) and (2, 3) are different points.

problem.en: In which quadrant does the point (−4, 5) lie? Give the abscissa and ordinate.

text.en: The abscissa is the x-coordinate, which is −4.
The ordinate is the y-coordinate, which is 5.
x is negative and y is positive, so the point is in Quadrant II.

prompt.en: A friend says (3, 2) and (2, 3) are the same point. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: The first number is always x
